No, that statement is not accurate.

Here is the correct information:

*   **Switzerland as a whole (federal level):** Swiss women gained the right to vote in federal elections in **1971**. This was the result of a national referendum held on February 7, 1971, in which Swiss men voted to grant women suffrage. Switzerland was one of the last countries in Europe to do so.

*   **Cantonal level:** The situation varied significantly among the cantons before 1971. Some cantons had already granted women the vote earlier (e.g., Vaud in 1959, Neuchâtel in 1950), while others did not allow it until 1971. Therefore, it was **not** the case that all cantons had already voted uniformly in favor of women's suffrage in 1971. The federal vote in 1971 was necessary to ensure uniformity across the country, as some conservative cantons had previously resisted extending voting rights to women.

In summary, women in Switzerland gained federal voting rights in **1971**, not 1981, and not all cantons had already granted those rights uniformly by 1971.
